The glyphosate toxicity studies you're not allowed to see

The report found that industry's own studies conducted in the 1980s and 1990s showed that glyphosate causes birth defects in experimental animals.

While the industry studies themselves are held by the German government and remain secret, the Earth Open Source authors examined Germany's summary report on the studies, which is in the public domain.

The Earth Open Source authors were surprised to find that the German regulator consistently dismissed evidence of birth defects using unscientific reasoning.

For example, the German regulator introduced irrelevant "historical control data" to dilute out the malformations seen in exposed groups of animals, enabling a false conclusion of no effect from glyphosate exposure. It also creatively redefined a known skeletal malformation as "rather a developmental variation than a malformation".

I once hired a redditor last year to set up reddit for me (as we all, know reddit is 'open' source). He was pretty good at it (as he is in touch with one of the reddit devs) and he had it set up within a day.

However, when I made the site 'live', it was flooded with spammers. When I asked him about it, he mentioned that the anti-spam feature for reddit is proprietary and that it hasn't been shared with the public - his explanation being that spammers would abuse reddit, if the anti-spam feature was made 'open'.

In this regards, is WhoaVerse (rather /u/atko) planning to keep some features 'closed' e.g. Anti-spam? Also, what anti-spam feature is WhoaVerse using as I don't see any 'report' button or any spam posts at all? From what I gather, the only anti-spam feature that I have noticed is the necessity for users to make at least one comment etc to be able to post things.
Is WhoaVerse planning to make any 'features' proprietary? And an anti-spam feature question.

There are currently no proprietary features (except for a console tool which re-ranks submissions as a scheduled task) and everything is in our github repository, but as we evolve, it is possible that some spam shields get developed privately. We currently use google recaptcha and a few other mechanisms to help prevent spam and moderators (all volunteers) are working hard to fight off any spam that may bypass our shields. We will do our best to incorporate spam filters into configurable modules.
